mcqs.question: A force of 200 N is applied uniformly on a metal rod having a cross‑sectional area of 0.5 m². Which of the following gives the correct value of the stress produced in the rod?
mcqs.explanation: Stress is defined as the internal restoring force per unit area, σ = F/A. Here F = 200 N and A = 0.5 m², so σ = 200/0.5 = 400 N/m². Option B uses the correct division; the other options misuse multiplication, invert the ratio, or add unrelated quantities.

mcqs.question: A cylindrical steel bar is pulled along its length by a force of 10 kN. Which description best characterizes the type of stress acting in the bar?
mcqs.explanation: When a force is applied parallel to the axis of a bar, the internal force acts normal to the cross‑section, producing longitudinal or tensile stress. Shear stress acts parallel to the area, bulk stress is isotropic, and bending stress varies across the section.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes bulk stress from longitudinal stress in a solid?

options.A: Bulk stress acts equally in all directions, while longitudinal stress acts only along the direction of the applied force.
options.B: Bulk stress is caused by shear forces, whereas longitudinal stress is caused by normal forces.
options.C: Bulk stress results in change of volume, longitudinal stress results in change of shape only.
options.D: Bulk stress is measured in N·m, longitudinal stress in N/m².

mcqs.answer: Bulk stress acts equally in all directions, while longitudinal stress acts only along the direction of the applied force.
mcqs.explanation: Bulk (hydrostatic) stress is isotropic—same magnitude on all faces—so it tends to change volume. Longitudinal stress is uniaxial, acting only along the line of the applied normal force, affecting length. Options B, C, D contain inaccurate descriptions.

mcqs.question: In a rectangular block subjected to forces acting parallel to its faces, the stress that tends to cause layers to slide over each other is called:
mcqs.explanation: Shear (tangential) stress acts parallel to the surface and tries to slide one layer over another. Longitudinal (tensile/compressive) stress acts normal to the area, bulk stress is isotropic, and tensile stress is a type of longitudinal stress.

mcqs.question: Stress in a material is defined as:
mcqs.explanation: By definition, stress σ = F/A, where F is the internal restoring force and A is the area over which it acts. The other options describe different physical quantities (pressure, energy density, strain).

mcqs.question: A force of 50 N is applied on a wooden block having an area of 0.25 m². What is the stress produced?
mcqs.explanation: Stress σ = F/A = 50 N ÷ 0.25 m² = 200 N/m². Option A is the correct calculation; the others arise from incorrect division or omission of the division step.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines longitudinal stress and distinguishes it from tangential stress?

options.A: Longitudinal stress acts normal to the cross‑section, while tangential stress acts parallel to the cross‑section.
options.B: Longitudinal stress acts parallel to the surface, while tangential stress acts normal.
options.C: Both are the same type of stress but differ in magnitude.
options.D: Longitudinal stress is always compressive, tangential always tensile.

mcqs.answer: Longitudinal stress acts normal to the cross‑section, while tangential stress acts parallel to the cross‑section.
mcqs.explanation: Longitudinal (normal) stress is perpendicular to the area, arising from pulling or compressing along the length. Tangential (shear) stress is parallel to the area, causing sliding. Options B, C, D misstate the directions or nature of the stresses.

mcqs.question: A deep‑sea submersible experiences a uniform external pressure of 5 MPa from all sides. The stress experienced by its hull is an example of:
mcqs.explanation: Uniform pressure acting equally in all directions produces hydrostatic or bulk stress, which tends to change volume but not shape. The other stress types involve directional forces or bending moments, not isotropic pressure.
